predecessors.name: Xiongnu
predecessors.text: the steppe north of the Gobi, the chanyu's court, seized in the civil war of 57-54 BCE

successors.name: Xiongnu
successors.text: the steppe north of the Gobi, left to Huhanye in 49 BCE

successors.name: Kangju
successors.text: the fortress 'on the Dulaishui River', possibly the Ili or Talas, built by the Kangju for Zhizhi

capitals.name: Chanyu's court north of the Gobi (Orkhon)

ledger.x: 56 BCE: Hutuwusi proclaims himself Zhizhi Chanyu.
49 BCE: Zhizhi takes the Jiankun and Dingling lands.
49 BCE: the court lands north of the Gobi are left to Huhanye, who had Han backing since 53 BCE and visited Chang'an in 51 and 49 BCE.
49 BCE: the court moves to the Jiankun lands on the upper Yenisei.
44 BCE: Zhizhi leaves the Yenisei for Kangju.
44 BCE: the court is the fortress on the Talas ('present-day Taraz, Kazakhstan').
36 BCE: Zhizhi is killed at the Battle of Zhizhi.

wars.name: Battle of Zhizhi
wars.outcome: Han victory: the city taken, Zhizhi killed and decapitated; the Western Regions' Han officers Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou acted on their own authority.

wars.name: Xiongnu civil war of the five chanyus
wars.outcome: Huhanye, backed by Han from 53 BCE, keeps the chanyu's title; Zhizhi withdraws to the Jiankun lands in 49 BCE.

certainty.note: A moving horde: every extent is approximate, the Talas base most of all.
